To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
narrative practices are of fundamental significance to cultural memory, and that narrative is a form of meaning construction that is based on the dialectics of forgetting and remembering.
narrative is a form of meaning construction that integrates various cultural symbol systems into one symbolic space, and that this space is a symbolic space of cultural memory.
(1) narrative is a cultural-historical practice, and (2) it is a mnemonic practice that combines remembering and forgetting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the past can be made to appear as the present, and how the present is made to appear as a part of the past.
the cultural-historical conditions of individual memory and with the ways in which these are reflected and shaped in cultural memory.
the question of how the past is represented in cultural discourse and how this past is made present and future in the present.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
narrative practices are a central means of cultural remembering and forgetting.
the cultural-historical perspective on narrative as cultural memory is able to explain how individual and collective remembering and forgetting is accomplished in a specific cultural context.
narrative is a cultural form that allows the integration of various cultural symbol systems into a symbolic space of meaning construction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
memory is not a cognitive process but a cultural practice.
narrative is the most important means of cultural memory, and that it is a means for the construction of cultural identities.
narrative is a form of cultural memory, a form of meaning construction, and a form of social interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
narrative, as a form of cultural memory, is not just a way of representing past events; it also serves as a medium for the production of new meaning.
the dialectics of forgetting and remembering are an inherent feature of cultural memory and are crucial for its function.
remembering is always a cultural practice, and as such, it is a practice of forgetting as well.
